newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian paper says 79 people died in riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian paper says 79 people died in riots.

text.p: A local Indonesian-language newspaper in Banjarmasin said on Sunday 79 people died in riots in the South Kalimantan capital on Borneo island on Friday, 75 of them in a gutted shopping complex.

The newspaper Dinamika Berita said 100 people were injured in the violence which swept the city of 400,000 people on the last day of campaigning for Indonesia's national and local elections next Thursday.
A five-day cooling off period started on Saturday and Banjarmasin was quiet following an overnight curfew on Saturday night.
Dinamika Berita quoted Banjarmasin's police chief Lieutenant-Colonel Preidi Tjiptoadi as the source of its information.
The newspaper said six government buildings, nine banks, two hotels, six restaurants and a number of shops and houses were destroyed in the violence.
It said 75 people died in the multi-level Mitra Plaza shopping complex of small shops. It said two other people died in the gutted Sarikaya supermarket, and another two died of stab wounds.
There was no immediate independent official comment.
The bodies were taken to the Ulin general hospital, where the injured were also being treated.
A local resident told Reuters the 75 who died in Mitra Plaza were apparently trapped when flames swept through the complex after dark following looting. It was not known how the fire started.
The violence erupted following clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar party campaigning in the city and angry crowds emerging from mosques after Friday prayers.

A tape of an interview given by Indonesia's Kalimantan military commander Major-General Namori Anoem and obtained by Reuters had him saying it was important to note that people had been looting the shopping complex.
He said 181 people had been detained by police.
